stories.headline: DOJ sends grand jury subpoenas to Philadelphia DA Krasner after judge's referral, sources say
stories.note: Progressive Philly DA Larry Krasner, a hero of the soft-on-crime left, is now facing federal grand jury subpoenas over possible obstruction.
body: The Justice Department has sent grand jury subpoenas to the office of Philadelphia District Attorney Larry Krasner, a Democrat, according to two sources who spoke to Fox News. They said the subpoenas involve possible obstruction of justice tied to how cases were handled in front of federal judges.

The move follows a referral from U.S. District Judge Paul Diamond more than a month ago. Diamond sent Krasner and his top deputy, Matthew Stiegler, to the DOJ for a possible criminal investigation, saying evidence in a murder conviction case could amount to false statements, perjury, obstruction and conspiracy. Neither man has been charged.

The fight centers on Dennis Johnson, who was convicted in 2009 of killing Kenyatta Smith. Krasner's office argued in 2022 that Johnson deserved habeas relief, and the judge later found that Krasner and Stiegler pushed prosecutors to give the court a false story and that Krasner warned staff of "consequences" if they flagged an internal conflict. Diamond removed both men from the case.
Krasner's office didn't respond to Fox right away, and the DOJ declined to comment. When the judge ruled, Krasner said he would "vigorously disagree" with the findings and planned to appeal.

Why it matters: Krasner has been one of the most prominent progressive prosecutors in the country. A federal grand jury probe, sparked by a judge's own findings, gives Republicans fresh ammunition in their case against soft-on-crime Democratic DAs.

stories.headline: Ilhan Omar's sister questioned by feds after dramatic DC home raid
stories.note: The immigration fraud probe into Rep. Ilhan Omar keeps widening, with her sister now questioned by federal investigators.
body: Rep. Ilhan Omar's older sister, Sahra Noor, was questioned by federal investigators last week as part of an immigration fraud probe into the congresswoman, three sources told Fox News Digital. They said Noor spoke with investigators voluntarily after last Monday's raid on Omar's Washington home.

Homeland Security Investigations executed a search warrant at the home around 6 a.m. that day. Investigators are looking at whether Omar or her father put false information on her citizenship paperwork, and border czar Tom Homan has said proven allegations could lead to denaturalization. The Wall Street Journal reported her phone, passport and computer were seized, and The New York Times reported about a dozen people, including relatives, have been subpoenaed.
Noor, who lives in Kenya and has been in the U.S. promoting a memoir, canceled a book event in Rochester, Minnesota, last week. A local bookstore said at the time it was due to a "family emergency."

Omar hasn't been seen publicly since the raid. On X, she called it "an outrageous abuse of power" and said she had done nothing wrong, and her lawyers have asked the DOJ to return some seized property. Vice President JD Vance told Fox the investigation isn't political and that the facts will drive it.
Why it matters: The probe is moving beyond Omar herself to her family, which keeps one of the Democrats' most polarizing members in the headlines just two weeks before the midterms.

stories.headline: Manchin bucks Schumer, throws support behind Republican Democrats want to oust
stories.note: Joe Manchin is heading to Maine to campaign for GOP Sen. Susan Collins, a direct snub of Schumer's top Senate target.
body: Former Sen. Joe Manchin, who left the Democratic Party to become an independent before retiring, is traveling to Maine on Wednesday to campaign for Republican Sen. Susan Collins, her campaign confirmed to Fox News Digital.

Collins is in a close race for a sixth term against Democrat Troy Jackson, a former state senator. Democrats have tried to paint her as a rubber stamp for President Trump, though she has broken with him at times, including on the "one big, beautiful bill."

Manchin, who served alongside Collins his whole Senate career, said he wants Maine voters to see her bipartisan record, from his infrastructure package under President Biden to blocking an Obamacare repeal. "She is not a Trump senator," he said.

Meanwhile Jackson has been joined by progressive stars Elizabeth Warren and Bernie Sanders, with Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez due in Maine the day after Manchin. A Collins spokeswoman said those visits tell voters "exactly how he would govern." Manchin has long clashed with Schumer and wrote in his memoir that he wanted Republicans to win the Senate in 2024 to protect the filibuster.

Why it matters: Maine is one of the Democrats' best chances to flip a Senate seat. Having a former Democratic senator vouch for Collins undercuts their main attack line and is a public embarrassment for Schumer.

stories.headline: Walz-era fraud scandal takes center stage as Klobuchar, GOP rival clash in debate: 'Why didn't you do more?'
stories.note: Republican Lisa Demuth put Amy Klobuchar on defense over Minnesota's Walz-era fraud scandal in their first governor's race debate.
body: Democratic Sen. Amy Klobuchar and Republican state House Speaker Lisa Demuth met for their first debate in the race to replace Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz, and the state's huge fraud scandal dominated the first half.

The pandemic-era welfare fraud schemes drained hundreds of millions, and possibly billions, of taxpayer dollars and helped push Walz to drop his re-election bid. Demuth tied Klobuchar to that record, asking why she didn't press the governor or show up at a Senate Judiciary hearing on the fraud. "Why didn't you do more," she asked.

Klobuchar said she "would have caught that fraud" and that once it became public she asked the Justice Department for more resources, which she said led to more federal prosecutors on the case. She said the hearing in question was a subcommittee she doesn't sit on.

Demuth also promised to fire every state commissioner for a fresh start and blamed Obamacare for soaring health costs. Both candidates ruled out tax hikes. Polls show Klobuchar ahead by high single digits, and the Fox News Power Rankings rate the race Likely Democrat.

Why it matters: Demuth is trying to become Minnesota's first Republican governor elected in 20 years. Keeping the Walz fraud scandal front and center is the GOP's best shot at making a blue state competitive.

stories.headline: Talarico skips Bernie Sanders rally in Texas, campaigns separately as Senate race heats up
stories.note: Texas Democrat James Talarico skipped Bernie Sanders' El Paso rally to campaign elsewhere, keeping the far left at arm's length.
body: Democratic Texas Senate candidate James Talarico skipped Monday night's El Paso rally headlined by Sen. Bernie Sanders, holding his own events hundreds of miles away in Denton and Fort Worth instead.

Sanders shared the stage with Beto O'Rourke and Democratic Reps. Greg Casar and Veronica Escobar as early voting opened. O'Rourke and Casar talked up Talarico, but Sanders never mentioned him by name and focused on billionaire donors.

At his Fort Worth rally, Talarico went after Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton and Elon Musk over money in politics. He also pitched himself as above party lines, saying the race "shouldn't be about the Democratic Party or the Republican Party."
Talarico and Paxton are running for the seat Republican Sen. John Cornyn is leaving, and Democrats are hoping for their first Texas Senate win since 1988. Election Day is Nov. 3.

Why it matters: When a Democrat in a close Texas race won't appear with the party's most famous progressive, it shows how much of a liability the far left is in red states, a gap Republicans can keep pointing to.

stories.headline: Trump puts fraudsters on notice with $25M whistleblower program offering cash for tips that deliver
stories.note: Trump and Vance are launching a $25 million program that pays tipsters who help convict people stealing taxpayer money.
body: President Trump and Vice President JD Vance are set to unveil a $25 million Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program in the Oval Office on Tuesday afternoon, a White House official told Fox News Digital.

Tipsters could earn up to $30,000 if their information leads to a fraud conviction or a significant federal enforcement action. Just filing a tip won't qualify. The Justice Department will run the program, and tips will go through fraud.gov.

Trump also plans to give independent journalist Nick Shirley a $10,000 check for his videos questioning whether several Somali-run Minnesota daycares were real businesses. The White House credits his reporting with bringing in FBI and DHS resources that led to investigations and charges. One former daycare CEO featured in his video pleaded guilty in July to stealing more than $4.6 million in child care claims plus $850,000 tied to the Feeding Our Future scandal.

White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said the administration has "zero tolerance for individuals who steal from Americans." The program builds on the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud that Trump created in March, chaired by Vance.

Why it matters: Fraud in taxpayer programs, especially Minnesota's under Democratic leadership, has become a major GOP theme. Putting cash rewards behind it two weeks before the midterms keeps the issue in front of voters.
